correctness.rationale: Independent analytic reconstruction: on input degree k the weight numerator is h! binom(k-j+h,h) for k≥j and zero otherwise, with denominator sqrt((k+2h)!/k!). Pascal's identity, also at k=j with the cutoff, gives (−1)^r h! binom(k-j+h-r,h-r) for k≥j, r≤h, then (−1)^(h+1) h! at k=j only. Thus the normalized matrix unit has the stated sign and scale. The lower differences have absolute tail weights asymptotic to h!/(h-r)! times k^(−r). Orthogonality makes singular values their decreasing rearrangement, which preserves the power asymptotic by tail counting. Summability and the endpoint logarithmic coefficient follow. The units span the finitely supported weights; their closure is c0, and one generator differs from the constant-weight shift by a c0 sequence. Finite rank requires the tail polynomial to vanish, hence all moments through h vanish by triangularity, which excludes at most h+1 distinct indices by Vandermonde. The finite frozen checker was inspected, not executed; the analytic check suffices.
